searches.reason: Develop practical, architecture-aware interventions that test whether rankings depend on recent repeated interests or isolated old purchases. Measure paired rank changes and uncertainty, connect failures to sequence representations and training objectives, and treat perturbations as sensitivity evidence rather than proof of user intent.

searches.reason: Find methods to distinguish broad similarity from supported compatibility, complementary purchases, and potentially satisfied durable needs using only histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions. Seek evidence-grounded probes with explicit unknown states; missing prerequisites or uncertain relevance must not become fabricated incompatibilities or dislikes.
searches.query: recommendation diagnostics purchase intent complement substitute compatibility prerequisite evidence product titles descriptions interaction history selective prediction abstention 2024 2025 2026

searches.reason: Establish whether diagnostic signals predict actual ranking failures across all four datasets. Seek affordable calibration against the pinned validation HR@10, full-catalog unseen-item audits for the twenty training users, popularity-stratified hard negatives, and user-bootstrap uncertainty; avoid tuning diagnostic thresholds to the same examples used to validate them.
